A Spanish court has sentenced a football fan to 11 months in prison for racially abusing Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe during a La Liga match against Real Oviedo in August 2025. Real Madrid disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the Second Section of the Provincial Court of Asturias found the individual guilty of a hate crime over racist insults directed at Mbappe during the fixture at the Carlos Tartiere Stadium on August 24, 2025. The club said the sentence also included disqualification penalties and a financial fine. “The suspension of the prison sentence is conditional upon the individual not attending football stadiums hosting official sports competitions for a period of two years,” the statement said. Real Madrid said the latest ruling added to previous criminal convictions over racist abuse directed at its players at the Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas and José Zorrilla stadiums. PUNCH Online reports that the incident occurred in the 37th minute of the match, shortly after Mbappe scored Real Madrid’s opening goal in their 3-0 victory. The supporter reportedly made monkey gestures and noises directed at the French forward as he celebrated with his teammates. The incident was captured on video and subsequently circulated on television and social media, drawing widespread condemnation. La Liga reported the incident to the relevant football authorities and later expanded its complaint to include racist noises directed at Brazilian forward Vinicius Junior when he came on as a substitute in the 63rd minute. Spanish police arrested a Real Oviedo supporter on September 10, 2025, after identifying him through an analysis of video footage from the match. He was investigated for alleged offences against moral integrity and hate crime. Real Oviedo subsequently apologised to Mbappe and Real Madrid over the incident, saying it would take appropriate action against the supporter.
